covers: LIST_SEARCH_RULE: look before you add, every time
LOG_PROMPT: 'save it' about a measure they already have means log the check-in
add_measure: never a second copy under a different id
expected_behavior: The user names a measure that is already in their list and asks whether they have it. The agent must look rather than guess, say it is already there, and then read 'save it' as the check-in it is -- logging the situation for that measure. It must not write a second copy of a measure it has just confirmed exists.
notes: Filed Tier 2 and failing on 2026-09-26; moved to Tier 1 the same day when the fix turned it green. Original finding: Found by the first play-then-freeze drafting pass: the agent added a near-duplicate of a measure it had just called 'already on your list', and logged nothing. Turns rewritten the same day -- the drafted ones opened with 'lets do the guided reset', which only makes sense if the agent offered it, and on the next run it had not. The authoring rule says turns must survive any question order, and those did not. These reach the same claim without presupposing anything. A fourth turn was added after the second run: the agent correctly ASKS the logging question before writing (CARD_RULES: ask first, the card carries the wording), and three turns gave it no turn in which to be answered. The case was failing on its own shape, not on the agent.

ok good. you can save it

covers: STATION_BASE: be honest about what actually happened
STATION_BASE: never describe something that was not returned to you
expected_behavior: Nothing has been written. The agent must say so plainly -- it can see its own tool receipts and knows no write happened. It must not say it cannot tell, and it must not describe any part of the app it has not been told exists.
notes: Filed Tier 2 and failing on 2026-09-26; moved to Tier 1 the same day when the fix turned it green -- the agent now answers 'No, nothing was saved.' Original finding: Drafted by playing the brief. The agent answered 'I don't have access to any files or a log view, so I can't see whether what you typed was saved' and then told the user to look for a 'History' tab. Two problems: it does know -- nothing was written and the receipts say so -- and the History tab does not exist in either client. Inventing UI is a fabrication the fabrication evaluator cannot catch, because the claim is about the app rather than about the log. Note that the expect block cannot assert the text: what was wrong here lives in the reply, and the deterministic fields only say that nothing was written -- which was true while the bug was live. The prompt rules pinned in tests/test_prompts.py are what actually guard it.

covers: FEEDBACK_PROMPT: respect what the user said they wanted from the conversation
no check-in is started for someone who has declined one
expected_behavior: The user is chatting and says twice that they do not want to check in. The agent should answer them like a person and stop asking for energy and goal. A negative case: it passes by the agent not acting.
notes: TIER 2, failing when written (2026-09-26). Drafted by playing the brief. The user deflected three times -- 'skip the check in lol', 'nope skipping again' -- and the agent asked for energy every single turn. The rule about respecting what the user wants lives in FEEDBACK_PROMPT, and an off-topic message never reaches that station: with energy, goal and situation unset it routes to `ask`, whose whole job is to collect them and which has no instruction for someone who does not want to.
